info.title: KaleidoSwap Maker API
info.description: Public HTTP API of the KaleidoSwap maker. Wire-compatible with the Boltz `/v2` protocol for submarine, reverse, and chain swaps, with KaleidoSwap additions (RGB, atomic swaps, pay-through, LSPS1, swap credentials). Integrate through the Swap SDK where possible: it verifies every swap the maker proposes.

On-chain → on-chain. Send your preimage hash, a claim public key, a refund public key, and one amount side (`userLockAmount` or `serverLockAmount`). The maker returns `lockupDetails` (where you lock) and `claimDetails` (where it locks for you). **Verify both against your keys before funding.** The response carries `swapAuth`, issued once.

post.description: Pay an address on another layer from Lightning. The maker returns a hold invoice; once it is paid, the maker sends the payout to `destination` and then settles the hold. Track it with `GET /v2/swap/{id}`. **The payout leg is controlled by the maker, not locked.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` to make retries safe; check `/v2/version` for `pay_through_idempotency_v1` first. Returns `503 pay_through_disabled` when the maker has not enabled it.

hash.description:
`SHA-256` over the canonical-JSON pair config. The `pairHash`
rate-lock.

pairId.description:
Exact pair key `POST /v2/quote` expects. Swap creation takes the
`from`/`to` currency symbols instead, so the maker resolves them to
whichever implementation is the direction's current default.

rate.description:
Display rate: output units per input unit, each asset counted in

get.description: The rate cards currently published for one swap type (`submarine`, `reverse`, or `chain`), as a map of `from → to → card`. A card carries the route's limits, fees, rate, and a `hash`. Pass that `hash` as `pairHash` when you create a swap to hold the maker to the terms you displayed.
The maker's version, build commit, and `capabilities`. Clients read `capabilities` to detect optional features, for example `pay_through_idempotency_v1`.

AtomicAmountDirection.description: Which amount of a quote request is fixed.

completion.description:
The finalized completion, handed out only once it was broadcast: the
taker needs it for `accept_swap_transfers`, and a transaction already
on the network is no option for anyone.

proposal.description:
rgb-lib's `OnchainSwapProposal`: the unsigned PSBT, for the taker's
`complete_swap_proposal`.

amount.description: Sats for BTC, the RGB contract's smallest unit for the asset.

assetId.description: The RGB contract of the RGB leg.

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds: the request must arrive before this.

networkFeeSat.description: Miner fee the taker funds on top of `fromAmount`, sats.

offerExpiresAt.description: Unix seconds: the completion must arrive before this.

serviceFee.description:
The maker's fee, in the output asset's units: sats, or the RGB
contract's.

toAmount.description: What the taker receives, net of the maker's fee.

challenge.description: 72 bytes hex: expiry (8-byte big endian Unix seconds), nonce, maker MAC.

signature.description:
BIP340 Schnorr signature (64 bytes hex) over SHA256(domain || canonical
26-byte uppercase swap ID || decoded 72-byte challenge). Domain is
`kaleidoswap/swap-auth-recovery/v1` followed by one zero byte.

ChainCreateResponse.description:
`POST /v2/swap/chain` response. Atomic Liquid pairs use Boltz's standard
`lockupDetails` + `claimDetails` shape. The optional flat fields preserve
the existing plain-send and Arkade extension responses.

payoutAmount.description: L-USDT amount the maker delivers once the BTC deposit confirms.

oneOf.description:
Present only for atomic chain pairs — the maker's L-USDT (or VHTLC)
lockup the taker claims revealing the preimage.

swapAuth.description:
Per-swap taker credential, 32 bytes hex — see
`swapAuth`. Chain swaps also need it on
`POST /v2/swap/chain/{id}/quote`.

height.description: Current chain tip height for the requested currency.

fee.description: sat/vByte estimate for the requested currency.

ChainQuoteAmount.description: Chain re-quote response and acceptance body.

amount.description: Destination amount in the asset's smallest integer unit. BTC and L-BTC therefore use satoshis.

oneOf.description:
Present on the Liquid HTLC server lockup; omitted for an Arkade
VHTLC (which is reparameterised by the taker, not script-shaped).

ChainSwapDetailsResponse.description: One side of the standard atomic Chain create response.

blindingKey.description:
`null` for Liquid; absent for Bitcoin, which has no such field. The maker mints its Liquid HTLC lockups **unconfidential** on
purpose, so no output blinding key exists to return: treat
`lockupAddress` as explicit — fund it with an unblinded output
where the taker funds, and build claims against an explicit
prevout where the taker claims.

CooperativeSignatureResponse.description:
Maker's partial-signature response on the cooperative claim/refund
endpoints (submarine refund, reverse claim, reverse refund, chain
claim, chain refund).

CreateChainRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v2/swap/chain` — Boltz-shaped, camelCase. Atomic routes return one HTLC description per side and do not require a
destination address at creation. The legacy plain-send route remains
address-driven for backward compatibility.

claimPublicKey.description:
Taker's 33-byte compressed **claim** pubkey for the Liquid side. Required for an *atomic* pair (the taker is the claim party on the
maker's L-USDT HTLC); ignored for the plain-send pair.

pairHash.description:
Optional `pairHash` rate-lock: the hash the taker quoted against. Verified against the pair's current rate card when present;
a mismatch is rejected with `400 pair_hash_mismatch`.

pairId.description:
Trading-pair key. Must resolve to a Chain pair in the engine —
Optional when `from`+`to` are given (stock Boltz SDK shape).

preimageHash.description:
The taker's BOLT11-style payment hash — `SHA256(preimage)`,
32 bytes hex. Goes into the BTC lockup's claim leaf; the maker
reveals the preimage at claim time.

refundPublicKey.description:
Taker's 33-byte compressed refund pubkey (BTC side). The maker
is the claim party on the BTC P2TR — taker refunds via script-
path if the maker fails to claim.

serverLockAmount.description:
Desired output-side amount; the maker inverse-quotes the canonical
input. Exactly one amount side is accepted.

userAddress.description:
Legacy plain-send destination. Atomic swaps construct the payout from
`claimDetails` after creation and therefore do not require it.

userLockAmount.description:
Input-side amount. Exactly one of this and `serverLockAmount` is
required.

oneOf.description: Optional HTTPS callback for status changes.

address.description:
Optional `host:port` the maker connects to before opening. If
omitted the client must already be peered with the maker.

client_balance_sat.description: Sats the LSP pushes to the client's side at open. Decimal string.

lsp_balance_sat.description: Inbound liquidity (sats) the client wants. Decimal string per spec.

public_key.description:
The client's node id (33-byte hex) — who the maker opens the
channel to.

refund_onchain_address.description: Where to refund the on-chain payment if the order fails.

asset.description:
Destination asset, when the layer carries more than one (Liquid:
`L-BTC` or `L-USDT`). Optional: with several routes to the layer the
maker delivers the one that does **not** convert the payer's bitcoin,
so naming an asset is how a payer asks for a conversion rather than
something they have to know to say.

destination.description:
Where the maker delivers: a Liquid address (confidential or explicit),
a Bitcoin address, or an Arkade address. The layer is inferred from
the address; it must belong to the maker's network.

invoiceAmount.description: Sats the payer sends over Lightning (the hold invoice's amount). Exactly one of `invoiceAmount` / `payoutAmount` is required.

pairHash.description:
Optional `pairHash` rate-lock against the reverse rate card the payer
quoted from; a mismatch is `400 pair_hash_mismatch`.

payoutAmount.description:
What the destination must receive, in the destination asset's smallest
unit. The maker inverts the rate card to find the invoice amount; the
delivered amount is the card's own net output for that input, so it
is at least this value.

oneOf.description: Optional HTTPS callback for status changes (Boltz `webhook` shape).

address.description:
Optional taker-owned Liquid destination for an L-BTC Magic Routing
Hint. Must be paired with `addressSignature`.

addressSignature.description: BIP-340 signature by `claimPublicKey` over SHA256(address UTF-8).

beneficiary.description:
A `kaleidoswap:` beneficiary handoff, in place of `preimageHash` +
`claimPublicKey`. This is how a payer pays **someone else** without having to take the
recipient's hash and key apart: the recipient's wallet emits one
string, the payer's passes it through. The maker checks the request's
network, expiry, destination layer and asset against the route it
resolves, and refuses to under-deliver what the recipient asked for.

bolt12Refund.description:
**BOLT12**: an `lnr1…` refund (a BOLT12 invoice request not tied to
an offer) the taker's node created for `invoiceAmount`. When present
the maker answers it — instead of minting a BOLT11 hold invoice —
with a BOLT12 invoice locked to `preimageHash`, holds it identically,
and delivers it back over the refund's onion-message paths; the
response's `invoice` is then that `lni1…`. The refund's amount must
equal `invoiceAmount`.

claimPublicKey.description:
The 33-byte compressed claim public key, hex — the key that claims
the maker's lockup. Optional only when `beneficiary` carries it.

from.description: Boltz: Lightning currency symbol (e.g. `"BTC"`). Combined with `to`.

invoiceAmount.description:
Amount, in sats, the taker pays via the hold invoice (Boltz
convention: `invoiceAmount` on Reverse). v0 BTC/BTC is 1:1 so this
is also what the taker receives on-chain.

pairHash.description:
Optional `pairHash` rate-lock: the hash the taker quoted against. Verified against the pair's current rate card when present;
a mismatch is rejected with `400 pair_hash_mismatch`.

pairId.description: Trading-pair key, e.g. `"BTC/BTC"`. Optional when `from`+`to` are given.

preimageHash.description:
The BOLT11 payment hash — `SHA256(preimage)`, 32 bytes hex. The hold
invoice is locked to this hash; whoever holds the preimage reveals it
on-chain when claiming the maker's lockup. Optional only when `beneficiary` carries it instead.

to.description: Boltz: on-chain currency symbol the taker receives (e.g. `"BTC"`).

oneOf.description: Optional HTTPS callback for status changes (Boltz `webhook` shape).

CreateSubmarineRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v2/swap/submarine` — Boltz-shaped, camelCase. Accepts both the maker's native shape (`pairId` + `preimageHash` +
`fromAmount`) and the **stock Boltz SDK** shape (`from` + `to` + `invoice`,
with the hash and on-chain amount derived server-side).

beneficiary.description:
A `kaleidoswap:` beneficiary handoff carrying the invoice to pay, in
place of `invoice`. This is how a payer funds a swap that pays **someone else**: the
recipient's wallet emits one string and the payer's passes it
through, rather than the payer knowing to pull an invoice out of it. The maker checks the request's network and expiry, and the swap is
atomic exactly as it always was — the lockup commits to the
recipient's payment hash, so the maker can only claim it by paying
them.

from.description:
Boltz: on-chain currency symbol (e.g. `"BTC"`). Combined with `to` into
a `pairId` when `pairId` is absent.

fromAmount.description:
Amount, in the from-asset's smallest unit, the taker will lock
on-chain. Optional for a BTC↔BTC submarine: derived from the invoice
amount + the pair's fees (Boltz `expectedAmount`). For a Liquid
submarine (L-BTC or L-USDT) the invoice is authoritative and this legacy
field is accepted only when it equals the canonical inverse quote.

invoice.description:
The BOLT11 invoice the taker wants paid over Lightning — the
maker pays it once the taker's lockup/VHTLC confirms, then claims
the lockup with the preimage the payment reveals. Its payment hash
must equal `preimage_hash`. Boltz-shaped submarine: the user
supplies the invoice to be settled.

invoiceAmount.description:
With `offer`: the Lightning amount, in sats, to request from a
variable-amount offer. Optional for a fixed-amount offer, and must
equal its amount when given. Rejected without `offer`.

offer.description:
**BOLT12 alternative to `invoice`**: an `lno1…` offer the taker wants
paid. The maker fetches an invoice from it at create time (without
paying), binds the swap to that invoice's payment hash — returned as
`preimageHash` — and releases the payment once the lockup confirms. Mutually exclusive with `invoice` and with an explicit `preimageHash`.

pairHash.description:
Optional `pairHash` rate-lock: the hash the taker quoted against. When present it's verified against the pair's current rate card and a
mismatch is rejected with `400 pair_hash_mismatch`.

pairId.description: Trading-pair key, e.g. `"BTC/BTC"`. Optional when `from`+`to` are given.

preimageHash.description: The taker's BOLT11 payment hash — `SHA256(preimage)`, 32 bytes hex. Optional: derived from `invoice` when absent (Boltz behaviour).

refundPublicKey.description: The taker's 33-byte compressed refund public key, hex.

oneOf.description:
Optional HTTPS callback for status changes (Boltz `webhook` shape). Persisted on the swap row; the dispatcher reads it on each
`SwapUpdate`.

details.description: Optional human-readable detail. Present on 4xx; absent on 5xx.

liquid.description:
Liquid venue state when configured. A degraded venue leaves process
liveness green so in-flight swaps can still reach this maker.

rgb.description:
RGB wallet state when configured: `ready` once online and synced,
`degraded` otherwise. Like `liquid`, never fails liveness.

blockHeight.description: Best block height the maker has observed on its LN backend.

haltReason.description:
The operator's reason for the halt, `null` when trading is live or
when the halt was engaged without one. Always present so a client
can read the key rather than probe for it.

halted.description:
`true` while the operator's trading kill switch is engaged. A halted maker refuses `/v2/quote` and every swap
create with `503 trading_halted` and publishes an empty pair
catalogue, but keeps settling in-flight swaps — so this is the
field a client polls to tell "stopped taking new business" apart
from "down".

network.description:
Bitcoin network the maker is configured for: `bitcoin`, `signet`,
`testnet`, `regtest`.

InternalHopRef.description: The swap a submarine pays in-process.

Lsps1Info.description:
`GET /v2/lsps1/info` — bLIP-51 options + maker node identity. Decimal
strings are LSPS1-spec verbatim (snake_case keys, sats as strings).

bip21.description: Signed direct-payment URI for the reverse-swap invoice.

signature.description: Schnorr signature by the reverse claim key over SHA256(address UTF-8).

NodesResponse.description: `GET /v2/nodes` response: currency → implementation → public node. The maker currently exposes one BTC Lightning node under the `LDK` key.

minerFees.description: Miner fee in sats (per the input chain).

percentage.description: Service fee as a percentage (Boltz convention: `0.5` = 50 bps).

maximalZeroConf.description:
Largest zero-conf-accepted amount. Always `0` — the swap engine has
no zero-conf acceptance path (every deposit waits for the configured
confirmation target regardless of amount), so the maker must never
advertise a non-zero value here.

minimal.description:
Smallest swap amount accepted, in the input asset's smallest unit
(an RGB asset's contract units).

expiresAt.description: Unix timestamp after which the unpaid hold invoice expires.

invoice.description: BOLT11 hold invoice the payer pays.

invoiceAmount.description: Sats the payer sends on Lightning.

pairId.description: The reverse pair the swap was priced on.

paymentHash.description:
The hold invoice's payment hash (hex). Maker-generated: the maker
settles the hold with the matching preimage after the payout is out.

payoutAmount.description: What the destination receives, in its asset's smallest unit.

swapAuth.description:
Per-swap taker credential, 32 bytes hex — see
`swapAuth`.

PayThroughFees.description:
The fee snapshot a pay-through was priced at, in the destination asset's
smallest unit.

PayoutStatus.description: The maker's leg of a pay-through swap, on `GET /v2/swap/{id}`.

reference.description: Destination-layer txid of the payout once broadcast, in display order.

PublicNodeInfo.description: One public Lightning node returned by `GET /v2/nodes`.

publicKey.description: Compressed Lightning node public key, hex encoded.

fromAmount.description:
Amount the taker would send, in the *input* asset's smallest units —
for an RGB asset, its contract's.

swapType.description:
Which swap family — `"submarine"` / `"reverse"` / `"chain"`. Pair
ids are scoped per kind: `BTC/BTC` exists in both Submarine and
Reverse as separate cards.

fees.description: Fee breakdown for this quote, in the output asset's units.

fromAmount.description:
Amount the taker would send, smallest unit of the input asset. An
RGB asset counts its contract's precision here and in every amount
below.

hash.description:
Pair-config hash — the `pairHash` the taker passes back on create
to rate-lock.

toAmount.description:
Amount the taker would receive after fees & spread; the same number
a create for `fromAmount` pays out.

validUntil.description: Unix-seconds timestamp past which the quote is stale.

accept.description: `true` → accept the re-quote and resume; `false` → reject and refund.

RestoreClaimDetails.description: Client-side claim material returned by swap restoration.

blindingKey.description:
Omitted for Liquid, whose lockups the maker mints **unconfidential**
on purpose, so no output blinding key exists to return; and for
Bitcoin, which has no such field.

RestoreDetailType.description: UTXO detail discriminator used by canonical Boltz restore responses.

RestoreRefundDetails.description: Client-side refund material returned by swap restoration.

blindingKey.description:
Omitted for Liquid, whose lockups the maker mints **unconfidential**
on purpose, so no output blinding key exists to return; and for
Bitcoin, which has no such field.

RestoreTransaction.description: Funding outpoint included once the relevant lockup exists.

preimageHash.description:
Canonical Boltz restore field. Older SDK bindings ignore this top-level
field, while newer clients need it to reconstruct submarine refunds.

RestoredSwapType.description: Swap kind in a restore result.

ReverseClaimRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v2/swap/reverse/{id}/claim` — Boltz-shaped, camelCase. Sighash sourcing: callers may either send the **raw unsigned tx**
(Boltz convention) — `transaction` (hex) + `index` — and the server
computes the BIP-341 key-path sighash, **or** send `signatureHash`
precomputed locally. The server prefers `transaction` when both are
present. Missing both is `400 missing_sighash`.

index.description:
Input index in the claim transaction. Defaults to 0 — most
cooperative claim txs only spend the single lockup input.

preimage.description:
The 32-byte preimage that satisfies the swap's `preimageHash`. The
maker uses this to settle the LN hold invoice.

pubNonce.description: The taker's MuSig2 pub nonce, 66 bytes hex.

signatureHash.description: 32-byte BIP-341 sighash the taker wants the maker to partial-sign. Optional when `transaction` is provided; required otherwise.

transaction.description:
Hex-encoded unsigned claim transaction. If present, the server
computes the sighash from this + `index` against the swap's
persisted lockup output, and any `signatureHash` is ignored.

blindingKey.description:
`null` for Liquid; absent for Bitcoin, which has no such field. The maker mints its Liquid HTLC lockups **unconfidential** on
purpose, so no output blinding key exists to return: treat
`lockupAddress` as explicit — fund it with an unblinded output
where the taker funds, and build claims against an explicit
prevout where the taker claims.

invoice.description: BOLT11 hold invoice the taker pays.

onchainAmount.description: On-chain amount the maker locks for the taker to claim.

oneOf.description:
**RGB routes only** (`to` on `rgb_l1`): how to find and claim the
RGB asset the maker locks in the swap tree's P2TR `lockupAddress`. `onchainAmount` is then the asset amount in the contract's units,
not sats.

swapAuth.description:
Per-swap taker credential, 32 bytes hex — see
`swapAuth`.

timeoutBlockHeight.description:
Block height (BTC/Liquid) or unix-ts (Arkade) at which the maker's
refund branch opens.

RgbLock.description:
The RGB lock of a swap whose deposit (submarine) or payout (reverse) is
an RGB asset in the swap tree's P2TR output. **Submarine:** the taker's rgb-lib `send` pays a witness recipient:
`recipientId` (the HTLC script) with `WitnessData { amount_sat: htlcSat,
blinding }`, assigning `amount` of `assetId`, and posts the consignment to
`transportEndpoints`. The maker pays the invoice once the lock has
`minConfirmations` and it holds exactly `amount` on the HTLC output; after
`timeoutBlockHeight` the taker can reclaim through the refund leaf, with a
colored spend (an uncolored one burns the asset). **Reverse:** once the hold invoice is paid (held) the maker's rgb-lib send
pays `htlcSat` to `scriptPubkey` assigning `amount` of `assetId`, and
posts the consignment to `transportEndpoints` under `recipientId`; the
lock txid is then on `GET /v2/swap/reverse/{id}/transaction`. The taker
accepts it with `blinding`, waits for `minConfirmations`, and claims
through the claim leaf with a colored spend of the HTLC alone (output 0 an
OP_RETURN commitment): `htlcSat` pays the claim at `claimFeeRate` and
leaves a 546-sat colored output, so the taker needs no BTC of their own. The claim reveals the preimage, which settles the hold. An uncolored
spend burns the asset. After `timeoutBlockHeight` the maker refunds.

amount.description:
Asset amount in the contract's smallest unit; equals `expectedAmount`
(submarine) or `onchainAmount` (reverse).

blinding.description:
Decimal blinding chosen by the maker. A string preserves all 63 bits
in JavaScript clients, whose JSON numbers lose precision above 2^53.

claimFeeRate.description: **Reverse only**: fee rate, sat/vB, `htlcSat` funds the claim at.

htlcSat.description:
Sats of the HTLC output: at least this (submarine); 546 plus the
claim fee at `claimFeeRate` (reverse).

minConfirmations.description:
Confirmations the lock needs before the other side acts on it; the
timeout leaves room for them and for the claim to confirm.

recipientId.description:
rgb-lib recipient id of the HTLC script: the proxy key of the lock
consignment.

scriptPubkey.description:
The HTLC output script (hex), the same P2TR as `address` /
`lockupAddress`.

transportEndpoints.description: RGB proxy the lock consignment is posted to.

acceptZeroConf.description:
Whether the maker accepts a 0-conf deposit. Always `false` — the swap
engine has no zero-conf path. Present because stock Boltz
clients require it (non-Option in their `CreateSubmarineResponse`).

address.description: P2TR lockup address (or `ark1…` VHTLC / `el1…` Liquid HTLC).

assetId.description: Swap asset for Liquid routes (L-USDT); omitted on BTC/Arkade routes.

bip21.description: BIP-21 funding URI for the taker's wallet (`bitcoin:<addr>?amount=<btc>`). Empty for Arkade/Liquid lockups, which are not `bitcoin:` URIs.

claimPublicKey.description: 33-byte compressed maker pubkey (hex) used in the MuSig2 aggregate.

expectedAmount.description: Amount the taker must lock on-chain (Boltz `expectedAmount`).

feeAssetId.description: Elements fee/policy asset for Liquid routes (L-BTC).

oneOf.description:
**Only when `invoice` is a hold invoice of this maker**: the swap that
minted it, which this one pays in-process instead of over Lightning. One hash binds both: the claim of that swap's lockup reveals the
preimage that lets the maker claim this deposit. Only an Arkade
deposit paying a reverse to an RGB lockup is admitted.

invoiceAmount.description:
**BOLT12 (`offer`) creates only**: the Lightning amount, in sats, the
fetched invoice is for and the maker will pay.

preimageHash.description:
**BOLT12 (`offer`) creates only**: the payment hash of the invoice the
maker fetched from the offer — the hash the lockup commits to, which
the taker could not know in advance. 32 bytes hex.

referralId.description:
Boltz compatibility field. The maker currently has no referral
attribution and returns JSON `null`.

oneOf.description:
**RGB routes only** (`from` on `rgb_l1`): how to lock the RGB asset in
the swap tree's P2TR `address`. `expectedAmount` is then the asset
amount in the contract's units, not sats.

timeoutBlockHeight.description:
Refund-leaf timelock (block height for BTC/Liquid; unix-ts for
Arkade — see the persisted form for which).

SubmarineRefundRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v2/swap/submarine/{id}/refund` — Boltz-shaped. The taker submits their `pubNonce` and the complete unsigned Bitcoin
refund transaction, or the versioned RGB PSBT request. Refunds do not
reveal a preimage. Bitcoin hash-only requests are no longer accepted.

pubNonce.description: The taker's MuSig2 pub nonce, 66 bytes hex.

signatureHash.description:
Deprecated for refunds. Hash-only requests return transaction_required;
ignored when a full transaction is provided.

transaction.description:
Hex-encoded unsigned refund transaction, required for Bitcoin refunds. The server computes the sighash from actual funding outputs via the Bitcoin
chain backend, validating that every input spends this swap's lockup.

SwapEventEntry.description:
One row of a swap's append-only event log. The log always opens with `created`: the creation event is written in the
same transaction as the order, so a swap cannot exist without it.

data.description:
Payment attempt number, rejection reason and certainty, or final
failure reason. Present only for submarine payment audit events.

kind.description:
The first entry of
every swap is `created`.

SwapLeaf.description:
One tapscript leaf — leaf-version byte (`196` / `0xc4` for elements,
`192` / `0xc0` for Bitcoin) plus the hex script.

index.description: Highest matching client derivation index, or `-1` when none matched.

SwapRestoreRequest.description:
XPUB search accepted by `POST /v2/swap/restore` and `/restore/index`. Supports the XPUB variant used by the TypeScript bindings; explicit
public-key and EVM-address variants are not supported.

derivationPath.description:
Child-key base path. Boltz defaults to `m/44/0/0/0`; SDK callers pass
`m` when the supplied XPUB is already the swap-account key.

gapLimit.description:
Consecutive unused-key scan limit. Boltz defaults to 50 and accepts
values in `1..=150`.

xpub.description: Extended public key from which client swap keys are derived.

paymentStatus.description: Customer-funding status, independent from the swap lifecycle.

SwapTransactionResponse.description: Boltz transaction lookup response for submarine/reverse swaps.

SwapTree.description: `swapTree` returned on every swap creation + status response.

capabilities.description: Explicit protocol features supported by this build.

WebhookConfig.description:
Opt-in HTTPS callbacks for a swap's status changes. ```json
"webhook": {
  "url": "https://merchant.example/callback",
  "hashSwapId": true,
  "status": ["transaction.confirmed", "invoice.paid"]
}
```

hashSwapId.description:
When `true`, the swap id in the callback payload is `SHA256(swap_id)`
— for merchants that don't want correlatable ids on the wire.

status.description:
`None` (the
field absent) means *every* transition is delivered.

PartnerAuth.description: Secret organization API key from the partner panel, for servers. Sent on swap creation as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` to attribute the swap to your organization. Optional; an invalid key is rejected. Never use it in client-side code.

OrgKey.name: X-Kaleido-Org-Key
OrgKey.description: Public organization key (64 hex characters) for client-side attribution. A label, not a credential. Sent on swap creation only. Never combine with `PartnerAuth`.

SwapAuth.name: X-Swap-Auth
SwapAuth.description: Per-swap credential returned as `swapAuth` when the swap is created. Required on the routes that decide a live swap's outcome (re-quotes, cooperative refunds), so knowing the swap ID is not enough.
